bug_info.bug_desc: In lc_ctrl.sv, the alert vectors were assembled in reversed bit order. The live alert vector `alerts` had `otp_prog_error_q` in the high bit and `state_invalid_error_q` in the low bit, while both software and TAP `alert_test` vectors had `lc_programming_failure` in the high bit and `lc_state_failure` in the low bit. Since alert index 0 corresponds to the programming-failure alert and index 1 to the state-failure alert, this swapped the two alert senders and made the `alert_test` bits trigger the wrong alert: writing bit 0 caused `lc_state_failure` instead of `lc_programming_failure`, and writing bit 1 caused the programming-failure alert instead of the state-failure alert. The same misordering existed on the TAP path.
bug_info.fix_hint: Swap the order of the two concatenated alert entries in `alerts`, `alert_test`, and `tap_alert_test` so that bit 0 drives/selects the programming-failure alert and bit 1 drives/selects the state-failure alert. Ensure the live alert vector, software test path, and TAP test path all use the same enumeration order.
